budget_items.topic: Sims Cloud / burial-search software annual renewal
budget_items.what_was_said: The invoice covers cloud annual maintenance and burial-search hosting; Todd Holman argued the commission is paying extra for a "view-only" second license it does not need since he already has full access on his own computer, aside from death certificates and DD-214s. The item was postponed to the next meeting so the vendor bill could be broken out and checked.

budget_items.topic: North Cemetery back-lot expansion bid (Della Sorell/Delson Roy)
budget_items.what_was_said: The contractor's estimate was negotiated down by reducing the area and depth of the work; the commission discussed how much of its capital funds versus commission (sale-of-lots) money would cover it before committing to go to bid.

budget_items.topic: Perpetual care and sale-of-lots fund balances
budget_items.what_was_said: The board walked through the Munis account rows line by line to confirm the perpetual care principal and sale-of-lots cash available before committing money to the expansion.

Several seasonal hire candidates were interviewed and two were not ratified by the select board before a third accepted; a prior part-time worker returned and a new hire ("Mike Jr.") was in process. Hours must stay under a cap so the town does not have to provide health insurance.
The bill covers correcting a headstone naming error, cleaning and engraving, and marking an unmarked 1864 burial found in South Cemetery; funded from the sale-of-lots account.

budget_items.topic: Cemetery lot and burial fee increase
budget_items.what_was_said: The board compared its current fees to nearby towns (e.g. Groton) and agreed the current price is well below market, raising the one-lot price, the full-body and cremation opening fees, and the second niche-wall opening fee effective July 1, while leaving the Saturday service fee (which goes to the town's general fund, not the commission) unchanged.

budget_items.topic: Return of two North Cemetery lots (Asco family)
budget_items.what_was_said: A veteran's family with two North Cemetery lots asked to return them for a veterans' cemetery burial instead; the board discussed refunding at or near the original purchase price versus retaining perpetual-care money, depending on how long the lots were held.

minutes.headline: Cemetery Commission voted to raise lot, burial and cremation fees for the first time in years, effective July 1
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Cemetery Commission approved minutes, heard praise from a resident for improved cemetery upkeep, and got a DPW update on the North Cemetery back-lot expansion, committing up to $45,000 toward the bid. It also voted to raise the price of a cemetery lot and burial/cremation opening fees effective July 1, 2026, discussed dropping a duplicate cemetery software license to save money, and postponed that software decision to the next meeting.

what_happened.line: Commission voted to raise cemetery lot and burial/cremation opening fees, effective July 1, 2026 -- the first increase in years.
Commission committed funding, the amount as heard, from the sale-of-lots fund toward the North Cemetery back-lot expansion, to go out to bid.
Commission approved payment for headstone correction and engraving work, including marking an unmarked 1864 burial found in South Cemetery.
A decision on dropping a duplicate cemetery software license was postponed to the next meeting so the vendor bill could be broken out.
A veteran's family asked to return two North Cemetery lots for a veterans'-cemetery burial instead; the board asked for the request in writing before deciding on any refund.

why_it_matters: Anyone planning to buy a cemetery lot or a burial/cremation opening in Lunenburg will pay the new, higher fee starting July 1, 2026.
The back-lot expansion is funded from the sale-of-lots fund rather than the town's general tax levy, and is meant to add burial capacity before winter.
The postponed software decision and the lot-return request both return to the commission's next meeting, on July 30.
watch_next: Next Cemetery Commission meeting, July 30, 2026, 6:00 p.m. -- expected to resolve the Sims Cloud software license question
Written return request from the Asco family on two North Cemetery lots, to be reviewed before a refund decision

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.coverage: official minutes are a summary only
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the core dollar figures — the $45,000 back-lot expansion transfer, the $3,500 monument invoice, and the new $1,200/$500/$300/$300 fee schedule — but diverge sharply in scope: our minutes capture extensive discussion (fund balances, competing bid figures, the Asco lot-return request, vault/natural-burial research, staffing numbers, a next-meeting date) the official minutes omit entirely, while the official minutes record a public comment, Flag Burning Day recognition, and a Facebook-posting discussion absent from ours. The one item a reader should check first is whether the $750/$450 sale-of-lots/perpetual-care fee split was actually voted (official) or is still pending town confirmation (ours) — that's a real outcome conflict, not a captioning slip.
